subject: Priv VPC architecture review — propose windows and pre-call asks
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <a.chen@brightoakhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Priv VPC architecture review — propose windows and pre-call asks

Hi Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can make the architecture review productive: 

1) Summary from our discovery: BrightOak wants a private VPC/on-prem bridge for PHI workloads, preferred HSM integration for key management, strict egress controls, and a 99th-percentile latency target of ~120ms for inference.

2) What we'll cover in the 90-minute architecture review: topology options (VPC vs. air-gapped on-prem), network & firewall prerequisites, KMS/HSM integration patterns, deployment timelines, and rollback/fallback policies.

3) Action items for your team before the call (helps speed the discussion):
   - Share a primary network contact (IP allowlist owner) and preferred CIDR ranges
   - Confirm whether you can provide a jumpbox or if we should route via a secure VPN
   - Any high-level compliance docs to pre-read (SOC2-type scope, retention constraints)

Proposing three 90-minute windows (all PDT):
   Option A: Mon Sep 4, 10:00–11:30
   Option B: Tue Sep 5, 13:00–14:30
   Option C: Wed Sep 6, 08:30–10:00

If none of those work, send 2–3 slots that do and we'll adapt. I'm including Marissa (solutions engineering) to run the technical portions and Ben (CS) for operational questions.

Attaching a one-pager SOC2 overview and a short network prerequisites checklist for your network team. Also linking our Priv Deploy playbook.

Thanks — looking forward to locking a time.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SOC2_overview.pdf (summary), network_prereqs_checklist.xlsx (checklist)
From: Alex Chen <a.chen@brightoakhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightOak Health IT <it@brightoakhealth.com>, Rajiv Patel <r.patel@brightoakhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 16:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Priv VPC architecture review — propose windows and pre-call asks

Thanks Connor — that recap is perfect. We can definitely cover the items you listed. A couple quick notes from our side: 

- Rajiv (cc'd) is our CISO and wants to join the technical session for the HSM and network discussion.
- We will need details on your HSM integration options (cloud KMS vs. on-prem HSM) since our procurement prefers customer-managed keys in HSM when PHI is in scope.
- We have an IP allowlist process; I’ll confirm the exact CIDRs but we need your expected egress IP ranges or a plan to use a NAT/proxy we control.

Regarding proposed times — Option B (Tue Sep 5, 13:00 PDT) would work best for our engineering + security leads, but we need to confirm with Rajiv. If he can't make 13:00 PDT, we can do Option C (Wed Sep 6, 08:30 PDT).

I also asked our procurement to pull the standard vendor security questionnaire; I’ll share any required paperwork ahead of the meeting.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightOak Health
a.chen@brightoakhealth.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <a.chen@brightoakhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv VPC architecture review — propose windows and pre-call asks

Appreciate the quick response, Alex. Quick replies inline and a short agenda we’ll use if you confirm Tue 13:00 PDT: 

- HSM options: we’ll present two patterns — (1) Redwood-managed KMS with customer-supplied HSM-backed keys (preferred for most customers) and (2) full on-prem HSM where keys never leave your network. We’ll include expected integration points and role mappings.
- Egress IPs: if you prefer we can run from static NAT IPs that we document ahead of time; otherwise we can use a customer-controlled NAT/proxy.

Proposed agenda (90 mins):
  1) 10 min — introductions and success criteria
  2) 35 min — architecture topologies and tradeoffs
  3) 25 min — security controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs, data flow)
  4) 15 min — network prerequisites & IP allowlist mapping
  5) 5 min — next steps and owners

Marissa will run the architecture review and will bring a short diagram pack. Ben will cover production runbook and support SLAs.

If Tue Sep 5 13:00 PDT works for Rajiv, we’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda, pre-read links, and a short Go/No-Go checklist for your infra team.

Also: for procurement, I attached a short SOC2 overview you can share with your security team; happy to connect legal if you need a mutual NDA while reviewing deeper docs.

—Connor
